name: Purah
overview: Purah is a male servant of Gideon, mentioned briefly in the book of Judges. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. His role is primarily defined by his service to the judge Gideon during a critical moment in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Purah means 'branch' or 'imposing,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. There is no indication that his name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful connotation within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture only records Purah's relationship as a servant to Gideon. There are no further family connections or relationships documented beyond this service role.
scriptureSignificance: Purah's significance lies in his association with Gideon, one of Israel's prominent judges. As a servant to Gideon, Purah is part of the narrative that highlights God's deliverance of Israel through chosen leaders. Though his role is minor and not elaborated upon, his presence supports the historical and spiritual context of Gideon's leadership.
